deep.reconstruction:
NOTATION (mine). Riemann works with bilinear forms f = a·s·z + b·s + c·z + d. Writing f as the 2x2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], the quadratic invariant is D(f) = ad − bc, and its polarisation is <f,g> = a d' + a' d − b c' − b' c, so that <f,f> = 2D(f). All forms on the page are normalised to D = 1. The fixed forms are (1) = s − z and (2) = λ²s − z/λ². Both have D = 1, and <(1),(2)> = λ² + 1/λ² =: Λ. I also write M = μ² + 1/μ², N = ν² + 1/ν², L = λ² − 1/λ², K = (λ + 1/λ)² = Λ + 2.

Geometric reading (mine). In P^1×P^1 (a quadric surface in P^3), such forms are plane sections, i.e. conics. Over C these behave like circles in Möbius geometry. For normalised forms, <f,g> = 2 means the two conics touch: D(f − g) = 0. More generally √(<f,g> − 2) plays the role of a tangential distance; for example √(M − 2) = μ − 1/μ.

A. A form P = αsz + βs + γz + δ touching both (1) and (2).
- The conditions are <P,(1)> = β − γ = 2 and <P,(2)> = β/λ² − γλ² = 2.
- Solving: β = 2λ²/(λ²+1) and γ = −2/(λ²+1).
- D(P) = 1 then gives αδ = 1 + βγ = ((λ²−1)/(λ²+1))².
- Riemann picks α = δ = (λ²−1)/(λ²+1); the system leaves a one-parameter freedom and this is the symmetric choice.

Top right: the decomposition of P.
- He takes 2P/α = 2sz + 4λ²/(λ²−1)·s − 4/(λ²−1)·z + 2.
- He writes this as a sum of two degenerate forms, (s + 1/τ)(z + τ) + (s + 1/τ')(z + τ').
- Comparing coefficients: τ + τ' = 4λ²/(λ²−1) and ττ' = −λ². So τ satisfies τ² − 4λ²/(λ²−1)·τ − λ² = 0.
- The discriminant/4 is λ²(4λ²/(λ²−1)² + 1) = λ²((λ²+1)/(λ²−1))².
- Hence τ = 2λ²/(λ²−1) ± λ(λ²+1)/(λ²−1), i.e. τ = λ(λ+1)/(λ−1) and τ' = −λ(λ−1)/(λ+1).

B. A general form (3) = αsz + βs + γz + δ with D = 1, <(3),(1)> = M and <(3),(2)> = N.
- Linear solution: Lβ = λ²M − N and Lγ = M/λ² − N.
- L²αδ = L²(1 + βγ) = M² + N² + Λ² − ΛMN − 4.
- This factors as −(λ²−μ²ν²)(μ²−λ²ν²)(ν²−λ²μ²)(1−λ²μ²ν²)/(λ⁴μ⁴ν⁴). This is the Fricke-type trace polynomial x²+y²+z²−xyz−4 with x = a + 1/a etc.

Imposing that (3) also touches P: <(3),P> = 2.
- Written out: (λ²−1)/(λ²+1)·(α+δ) + 2β/(λ²+1) − 2λ²γ/(λ²+1) = 2.
- Using Lβ − λ²Lγ = (λ²−1)(M+N) this becomes L(α+δ)/2 = K − M − N, i.e. (λ+1/λ)² = L(α+δ)/2 + M + N.
- Then L²((α−δ)/2)² = (K − M − N)² − L²αδ = ΛMN + 2MN − 2Λ(M+N) − 4(M+N) + 4Λ + 8 = (Λ+2)(M−2)(N−2).
- Taking the root: L(α−δ)/2 = (λ+1/λ)(μ−1/μ)(ν−1/ν), up to a choice of sign.
- Adding and subtracting gives Lα and Lδ as products of four linear factors. Riemann writes:
  - Lα = −(λ+μν)(μ−λν)(ν−λμ)(1+λμν)/(λ²μ²ν²);
  - Lδ = (λ−μν)(μ+λν)(ν+λμ)(1−λμν)/(λ²μ²ν²).

C. Degenerate combinations.
- D((3) − μ²(1)) = 1 − μ²M + μ⁴ = 0, so this form is degenerate. Riemann computes:
  - L((3) − μ²(1)) = L(αsz + δ) + (λ²/μ² + μ²/λ² − N)·s + (λ²μ² + 1/(λ²μ²) − N)·z;
  - the s-coefficient factors as (λ²/μ²)(μ²/λ² − ν²)(μ²/λ² − 1/ν²);
  - the z-coefficient factors as (1/(λ²μ²))(λ²μ² − ν²)(λ²μ² − 1/ν²).
- Hence L((3) − μ²(1)) = αL·(s − A)(z + B), with A = (ν+λμ)(1−λμν)/((λ+μν)(μ−λν)) and B = (λ−μν)(μ+λν)/((ν−λμ)(1+λμν)). This is the splitting into the two rulings.
- The same is done for (3) − (1)/μ², which swaps the s and z coefficients.
- And for (3) − ν²(2): s-coefficient λ²(M − ν²λ² − 1/(ν²λ²)), z-coefficient (1/λ²)(M − ν²/λ² − λ²/ν²).

D. Two such forms (3) with (μ,ν) and (3') with (μ',ν'), both touching P. Riemann sets <(3),(3')> = λ'² + 1/λ'² and computes L²<(3),(3')>.
- The αδ' + α'δ part is ½[L(α+δ)L(α'+δ') − L(α−δ)L(α'−δ')]. This gives 2(M+N−K)(M'+N'−K) ± 2K(μ−1/μ)(ν−1/ν)(μ'−1/μ')(ν'−1/ν').
- The −(βγ' + β'γ) part gives −2MM' − 2NN' + Λ(MN' + M'N).
- Dividing by K, using L² = K(λ − 1/λ)²:
  MN' + M'N − 2(M + N + M' + N') + 2(λ+1/λ)² + 2(μ−1/μ)(ν−1/ν)(μ'−1/μ')(ν'−1/ν') = (λ − 1/λ)²(λ'² + 1/λ'²).
- Since 2(λ+1/λ)² − 8 = 2(λ−1/λ)², this is a perfect square. The result is the final line:
  (λ − 1/λ)(λ' − 1/λ') = (μ − 1/μ)(ν' − 1/ν') + (μ' − 1/μ')(ν − 1/ν).

Interpretation (mine). Write t(f,g) = √(<f,g> − 2). Then t(1,2) = λ − 1/λ, t(1,3) = μ − 1/μ, t(2,3) = ν − 1/ν, t(1,3') = μ' − 1/μ', t(2,3') = ν' − 1/ν', t(3,3') = λ' − 1/λ'. So the last line reads t12·t33' = t13·t23' + t13'·t23 for four 'circles' (1), (2), (3), (3') all touching a fifth one (P). That is Casey's theorem (generalised Ptolemy), here in the projective/complexified Möbius model of plane sections of a quadric.

This fits the next page, which contains Ptolemy-type identities such as (n−1/n)(m/r−r/m) + ... = 0 and relations among √(xy), √(zt), .... It is presumably aimed at relations of theta-type (square-root) quantities; the previous page counts theta characteristics.
errors: Overall sign of α and δ in part B. With the reference form taken exactly as written (α0 = δ0 = +(λ²−1)/(λ²+1)) and the root L(α−δ)/2 = +(λ+1/λ)(μ−1/μ)(ν−1/ν), one gets Lα = +(λ+μν)(μ−λν)(ν−λμ)(1+λμν)/(λ²μ²ν²) and Lδ = −(λ−μν)(μ+λν)(ν+λμ)(1−λμν)/(λ²μ²ν²). Numerical check at λ=2, μ=3, ν=5: Lα = +4.099 and Lδ = −59.90, whereas the page gives −4.099 and +59.90. Riemann's signs are those for the other root α0 = δ0 = −(λ²−1)/(λ²+1). The later factorisation (3) − μ²(1) = αL(s − A)(z + B) is written consistently with his own signs, so the slip is harmless for the final result.

In part D the sign in front of 2(λ+1/λ)²(μ−1/μ)(ν−1/ν)(μ'−1/μ')(ν'−1/ν') depends on the branch chosen for α' − δ'. A direct computation with the same branch for both forms gives a minus; the page's plus corresponds to opposite branches. The final Ptolemy/Casey relation is correct up to the corresponding sign choice.
The expansion line for L²((α−δ)/2)² is left incomplete on the page (dashes for omitted symmetric terms). The completed expression ΛMN + 2MN − 2Λ(M+N) − 4(M+N) + 4Λ + 8 does equal (Λ+2)(M−2)(N−2).
Choosing α = δ in part A is a free choice, not forced: only αδ is determined. This is not flagged on the page but is legitimate.

results.what: Normalised bilinear forms αsz+βs+γz+δ on P^1×P^1 with invariant αδ−βγ and its polarisation; tangency of conics expressed as <f,g> = 2
results.modern_name: Plane sections of a quadric / SL2-matrices with the determinant quadratic form (Möbius/Lie-sphere-type coordinates)
results.usually_credited_to: Plücker, Klein, Darboux (pentaspherical coordinates and quadric models, 1860s–1870s)

results.what: Factorisation M²+N²+Λ²−ΛMN−4 = −(λ²−μ²ν²)(μ²−λ²ν²)(ν²−λ²μ²)(1−λ²μ²ν²)/(λ⁴μ⁴ν⁴) with M = μ²+μ⁻², etc.
results.modern_name: Fricke–Vogt trace polynomial x²+y²+z²−xyz−4 factorised in eigenvalue parameters
results.usually_credited_to: Vogt (1889), Fricke (1896) in the trace context; the algebraic factorisation itself is elementary

results.what: Splitting of the degenerate forms (3) − μ²(1), (3) − μ⁻²(1), (3) − ν²(2) into products of linear factors (the two rulings)
results.modern_name: Factorisation of rank-one bilinear forms / tangent-plane sections of a quadric

results.what: For four conics (1), (2), (3), (3') all touching a fifth conic P, with tangential invariants t = √(<f,g>−2): (λ−1/λ)(λ'−1/λ') = (μ−1/μ)(ν'−1/ν') + (μ'−1/μ')(ν−1/ν)
results.modern_name: Casey's theorem (generalised Ptolemy theorem), in projective/complexified Möbius form
results.usually_credited_to: John Casey (1866); Ptolemy for the point case

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra is elementary and correct apart from sign bookkeeping. Read geometrically, it derives a Casey/Ptolemy-type relation for conic sections of a quadric touching a common conic. Casey's theorem appeared in 1866, Riemann's death year, and an independent projective version by Riemann is not known in the literature. It is, however, a short computation, plausibly auxiliary to theta-function relations, and the geometric interpretation is mine rather than stated on the page. So it is a notable unpublished detail, not a major result.

checkable.asserts: Solution of part A: β, γ satisfy both tangency conditions and αδ = ((λ²−1)/(λ²+1))² (expect [0,0,0])
Roots τ, τ' of the quadratic and the decomposition of 2P/α into two degenerate forms (expect [0,0,0])
Correct signs: Lα = +(λ+μν)(μ−λν)(ν−λμ)(1+λμν)/(λ²μ²ν²) and Lδ = −(λ−μν)(μ+λν)(ν+λμ)(1−λμν)/(λ²μ²ν²) for the + root; the page has both with opposite sign (expect [0,0])
Factorisations of the s- and z-coefficients of L((3) − μ²(1)) (expect [0,0])
(3) − μ²(1) splits as αL(s−A)(z+B), with A, B sign-adjusted to the corrected α (expect 0)
The penultimate equation is equivalent to (λ−1/λ)²(λ'−1/λ')² = [(μ−1/μ)(ν'−1/ν')+(μ'−1/μ')(ν−1/ν)]² (expect 0)
(1) and (2) are normalised (invariant 1) and have mutual invariant λ²+1/λ² (expect [1,1,0])

transcription_corrections: The first line after the two definitions is the auxiliary form P = αsz+βs+γz+δ (the label on the page may not be '1'); it is distinct from (1) = s − z.

In the line for L²((α−δ)/2)², the garbled '+2(μ²+1/μ²)ν²1/ν²' should read '+2(μ²+1/μ²)(ν²+1/ν²)', followed by elided symmetric terms '− · − ·' and '−4(μ²+1/μ²+ν²+1/ν² − λ² − 1/λ²) + 8' (dashes on the page).

In the line for (λ²−1/λ²)α, the first terms are crossed out and partly illegible; the surviving expression is ±[(μ−1/μ)² + (ν−1/ν)² − (λ+1/λ)² ∓ (λ+1/λ)(μ−1/μ)(ν−1/ν) + 4]. The printed '(μ+1/μ)²' should be '(μ−1/μ)²'.
In the bracketed expansion of part D, the factor (λ²+1/λ²) multiplies both (μ²+1/μ²)(ν'²+1/ν'²) and (μ'²+1/μ'²)(ν²+1/ν²).
In the last line, the final factor is (ν − 1/ν), unprimed (the page has a corrected letter there).
